column11: CLEAR enrols CT-confirmed bronchiectasis with at least 2 moderate or 1 severe exacerbations in 12 months and Pseudomonas aeruginosa cultured within 5 weeks (NCT07088926 eligibility). The share is from the US Bronchiectasis and NTM Research Registry, 2,950 adults (Lapinel NC et al., 'Characteristics of exacerbators in the US Bronchiectasis and NTM Research Registry: a cross-sectional study', ERJ Open Res 2024, doi:10.1183/23120541.00185-2024, PMID 39534769, PMC11551853): 438 patients (14.8%) had 2 exacerbations and 607 (20.6%) had 3 or more in the 2 years before enrolment, and P. aeruginosa infection was 23.4% and 35.2% in those groups. (438 x 0.234 + 607 x 0.352) / 2,950 = 316.2 / 2,950 = 0.107172, about 36,400 of the 340,000
column12: Judgement on the window: two exacerbations over two years is looser than the trial's two in one, which overstates; the trial's alternative of one severe exacerbation, which this leaves out, understates; and a specialist-centre registry is sicker than the claims population the pool counts, which overstates. A P. aeruginosa infection in the registry is not always the chronic colonisation the trial requires

column11: judgement, with the measured context: in the US registry only 10% of 740 patients without NTM were taking inhaled suppressive antibiotics, 68% of them with chronic P. aeruginosa (Henkle E et al., Chest 2017;152(6):1120-1127, doi:10.1016/j.chest.2017.04.167, PMID 28479113), so a maintenance therapy aimed at Pseudomonas has historically reached a small minority of the patients it fits
column12: the row to argue with. At 5% of the eligible pool started a year and Tezspire's 41% stopping, the steady-state stock is about 5,300 patients, roughly 15% of the eligible pool. The case for higher: Pseudomonas-colonised frequent exacerbators have no therapy aimed at the organism other than inhaled antibiotics, which are off label in the US for this disease. The case for lower: Brinsupri, an oral tablet with an approved label, will have been on sale for eight years by 2034, and an infusion every few weeks is a burden an oral drug is not. Nothing settles it but sales
